stories.headline: OpenAI reasoning model disproves Erdős's 80-year-old unit distance conjecture

key_facts.fact: An internal OpenAI general-purpose reasoning model disproved the planar unit distance conjecture, first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946, producing an infinite family of point sets that beats the long-assumed 'square grid' optimum with a polynomial improvement (n^(1+δ) for a fixed δ>0, versus the previously believed n^(1+o(1))).
key_facts.excerpt: An internal OpenAI model has disproved this longstanding conjecture, providing an infinite family of examples that yield a polynomial improvement. The proof has been checked by a group of external mathematicians.

key_facts.fact: The proof came from a new general-purpose reasoning model, not a system trained specifically for mathematics or theorem proving and not scaffolded for this problem; it surfaced while OpenAI was evaluating the model on a collection of Erdős problems.
key_facts.excerpt: The proof came from a new general-purpose reasoning model, rather than from a system trained specifically for mathematics... As part of a broader effort to test whether advanced models can contribute to frontier research, we evaluated it on a collection of Erdős problems.

key_facts.fact: The OpenAI team credited Lijie Chen with producing the proof using the internal model, and Mark Sellke and Mehtaab Sawhney with verifying correctness; a separate arXiv paper later made the exponent explicit, showing sets of n points with more than n^1.014 unit-distance pairs.
key_facts.excerpt: both conjectures were disproved by a team at OpenAI, consisting of Lijie Chen using an internal OpenAI model and Mark Sellke and Mehtaab Sawhney verifying correctness... We show that there are sets of n points in the plane... that contain more than n^{1.014} pairs of points separated by a distance exactly 1.

key_facts.fact: External mathematicians (Alon, Bloom, Gowers, Litt, Sawin, Shankar, Tsimerman, Wang and Matchett Wood) wrote a companion 'Remarks' paper presenting a human-digested version of the argument, which relies on tools from algebraic number theory; the AI proof was generated 'in one shot' and then refined through human interaction with Codex.
key_facts.excerpt: We present a short, digested, human-verified version of the recent OpenAI-generated counterexample to the Erdős unit distance conjecture... which was first mathematically generated in one shot by an internal model at OpenAI, and then expositionally refined through human interactions with Codex.

key_facts.fact: Fields medalist Tim Gowers called the result a milestone in AI mathematics, and observers framed it as the first time a prominent open math problem was solved autonomously by AI; mathematician Gil Kalai compared its potential significance to the 1976 computer-assisted proof of the four-color theorem.
key_facts.excerpt: Like the computer-based proof of the four color theorem in 1976 by Appel and Haken, this may well be a scientific landmark whose importance goes beyond combinatorics and beyond mathematics.

stories.headline: Anthropic projects $10.9B Q2 revenue and its first-ever operating profit

key_facts.fact: Anthropic told investors it is on track to generate about $10.9 billion in revenue in the second (June) quarter, more than double the $4.8 billion it booked in the first quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is on track to generate $10.9 billion in revenue during the second quarter... Anthropic generated $4.8 billion during the first quarter, the person said, meaning that its sales more than doubled in a matter of months.

key_facts.fact: Hitting that target would mark Anthropic's first profitable quarter, with roughly $559 million in operating income, a 130% quarter-over-quarter revenue jump.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is projected to achieve $10.9 billion in revenue for Q2, representing a 130% increase from $4.8 billion in Q1, which will result in its first operating profit of $559 million.

key_facts.fact: The single-quarter figure would exceed Anthropic's revenue for all of the prior year and implies an annualized run rate of roughly $44 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic projects $10.9 billion June quarter revenue and its first $559 million operating profit, implying a $44 billion annualized run rate during a funding round likely valuing it above OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: The figures were disclosed to investors as part of an ongoing funding round and were first reported by The Wall Street Journal; Anthropic declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal was first to report Anthropic's revenue figures.

key_facts.fact: The disclosure surfaced the same day as reports that OpenAI is preparing to file for an IPO, sharpening the rivalry narrative between the two leading AI labs.
key_facts.excerpt: According to sources, the figures about the probable profit appeared on the same day as reports that OpenAI is likely to file for an IPO soon. Anthropic declined to comment further.

key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is preparing to confidentially file a draft of its IPO prospectus as soon as Friday... working with banks including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to prepare to file in the coming days or weeks.

stories.headline: Stability AI releases Stable Audio 3.0 with six-minute songs and open weights

key_facts.fact: Stability AI released Stable Audio 3.0, a family of four models (three with open weights, one API-only) trained entirely on licensed data, capable of generating music tracks more than six minutes long.
key_facts.excerpt: We're releasing Stable Audio 3.0, a model family with open-weights music models that are trained on fully licensed data... Key innovations include variable-length generation up to six minutes, and full song composition on portable devices.

key_facts.fact: The medium and large models were trained on a mix of licensed audio from AudioSparx (806,284 audios) plus Creative Commons recordings from Freesound, with copyrighted material filtered out using a music tagger.
key_facts.excerpt: they are trained on a combination of licensed audio from production library AudioSparx (806,284 audios) and Creative Commons recordings from Freesound. To ensure no authorized copyrighted material ended up in the dataset... music recordings were filtered using a tagging tool.

key_facts.fact: Three variants (3.0 Small, 3.0 Small SFX and 3.0 Medium) are downloadable on Hugging Face while 3.0 Large is API-only; the company says 3.0 Small is the only model capable of full music composition on-device.
key_facts.excerpt: three of which ship with open weights. The models generate music tracks up to six minutes long and were trained entirely on licensed data... The largest model is only accessible through the Stability AI API.

key_facts.fact: With fully licensed training data and legal indemnification for enterprise customers, Stability is positioning itself against rivals Suno and Udio, which face music-industry copyright lawsuits.
key_facts.excerpt: With licensed training data and legal indemnification for enterprise customers, Stability AI is deliberately distancing itself from competitors currently facing copyright lawsuits... like Suno and Udio.

key_facts.fact: Users own the audio they generate and can commercialize it under the Stability AI Community License; organizations with more than $1M in annual revenue need an Enterprise License.
key_facts.excerpt: You own your outputs and can distribute and commercialize them under the Stability AI Community License, or the Enterprise License for organizations with more than $1M in revenue.

stories.headline: Microsoft open-sources RAMPART and Clarity, AI agent red-teaming and safety tools

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's AI Red Team open-sourced two tools: RAMPART, an agent test framework that encodes adversarial and benign scenarios as repeatable tests that run in CI, and Clarity, a structured 'sounding board' that helps teams decide whether they are building the right thing before writing code.
key_facts.excerpt: Today Microsoft is open-sourcing two tools designed to help engineers: Microsoft RAMPART, an agent test framework for encoding adversarial and benign scenarios as repeatable tests that can run in CI... and Clarity, a structured sounding board that helps teams figure out whether they are building the right thing before they write a single line of code.

key_facts.fact: RAMPART is built on top of PyRIT, Microsoft's open red-teaming automation framework, and is aimed at engineers building systems, letting them turn red-team findings and AI incidents into lasting regression coverage.
key_facts.excerpt: It is built on top of PyRIT, Microsoft's open automation framework for red teaming generative AI systems... Where PyRIT is optimized for black-box discovery by security researchers after the system is built, RAMPART is built for engineers as the system is being built.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft framed the release as making AI safety a continuous engineering discipline rather than a periodic checkpoint, motivated by the growing access and permissions that agents need to data like email, records and code repositories.
key_facts.excerpt: "We built these tools because we believe that AI safety has to become a continuous engineering discipline rather than a periodic checkpoint..." the AI Red team said today.

key_facts.fact: The company cited three reasons for investing in the tools: scaling red-teaming practices industry-wide, making incidents reproducible and verifying mitigations, and helping engineers think through the 'why' before the 'how' of building software.
key_facts.excerpt: the company pointed to three reasons that it's investing in these tools: To help scale red-teaming practices industry-wide, make incidents reproducible and verify mitigation techniques, and allow engineers to 'think through the why,' before the 'how' of software building.

stories.headline: AI startups raise across stages, from Exa's $250M round to seed deals for agent builders

key_facts.excerpt: Exa Labs Inc. today announced that it has raised $250 million... The round was led by Andersen Horowitz. It comes less than a year after Exa's previous raise, a $85 million Series B... The company is now valued at $2.2 billion.

key_facts.excerpt: Viktor... has raised a $75m Series A led by Accel... Viktor reached $15m in annualised recurring revenue in roughly ten weeks... more than 12,000 teams have now installed Viktor across Slack and Microsoft Teams.

stories.headline: Pentagon launches Cyber Command-NSA task force to deploy frontier AI in cyber ops

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon is standing up a task force spanning U.S. Cyber Command and the NSA to study how it can safely deploy leading AI models across its missions, including on 'high-side' systems holding the intelligence community's most sensitive secrets.
key_facts.excerpt: the task force will span Cyber Command and the NSA, and will study how the Pentagon can safely deploy leading AI models in all aspects of its missions... This includes assessing how AI models built by Silicon Valley tech giants can be used on 'high-side' systems bearing some of the intelligence community's most sensitive secrets.

key_facts.fact: The lead role was assigned to a commander at Cyber Command, which a former senior national security official said signals CYBERCOM is 'more in charge, with NSA in support.'
key_facts.excerpt: assigning the lead role to a commander at Cyber Command suggested that the combatant command 'is more in charge, with NSA in support.'

key_facts.fact: Officials argued AI tools are becoming essential for detecting threats, prioritizing vulnerabilities and conducting both defensive and offensive cyber operations faster than adversaries.
key_facts.excerpt: "AI tools are rapidly becoming essential for detecting threats, prioritizing vulnerabilities, accelerating decision making and conducting both defensive and offensive cyber operations faster than our adversaries," Moore said.

key_facts.fact: The task force is not directly connected to the forthcoming White House AI executive order, though both CYBERCOM and NSA are expected to play a central role in new cybersecurity efforts.
key_facts.excerpt: The task force is not directly connected to the forthcoming EO, although both Cyber Command and NSA are expected to play a central role in any new cybersecurity-related efforts.

key_facts.fact: The effort could increase pressure to lift the Defense Department's March 'supply chain risk' designation on Anthropic, whose Mythos model the company has said it is open to letting the government use in offensive cyber operations.
key_facts.excerpt: the company is open to allowing the U.S. government to use Mythos in offensive cyber operations. That is something the Pentagon is likely to explore — and it could create pressure within the Defense Department to lift the supply chain risk designation on Anthropic.
